gaps.explanation: Revenue detail is the Budgetary Comparison Schedule - Cash Basis - Total Primary Government (p20), which covers governmental and business-type together. Its governmental-tagged lines total 365,926 (Property 89,581, Federal 37,610, Pro-rate 209, Highway allocation and incentive 77,862 (= statement 77,262 + 600), Motor vehicle fees 5,690, Municipal equalization 21,172, State Other 10,980 (= homestead 5,331 + property tax credit 5,649), Motor vehicle 11,036, Sales tax 109,515, In lieu 2,271). The other governmental receipts on the statement p9 Total column - Franchise 3,483, Occupation 4,110, Carline 430, Charges for services 13,108, Lease fees/rentals 16,622, Fees permits licenses 1,004, Interest 27, Donations 5,380, Park Fund grants 16,500 (statement Grants 54,110 - Federal 37,610), Sale of assets 13,765, Insurance proceeds 58,847, Other revenues 7,837 = 141,113 = gap - are inside the single printed line 'Local Receipts: Other' 1,327,744 (detail index 10), which mixes governmental and business-type receipts with no printed breakdown and is tagged business-type. No line is missing; the printed schedule does not separate them, so no split is made.

Statement p10 prints Transfers Out by fund: General Fund (77,002), Street and Alley Fund (2,700); Adjustments column (p11) eliminates 58,452, Total (21,250). detail[] has no transfers out at all (the governmental expenditure detail comes from the p22 Schedule of Expenditures, which has no transfers; the budget schedule's governmental function lines that include transfers are not recorded). Added the two fund-column transfers out gross: 77,002 + 2,700 = 79,702. Schedule is then 79,702 vs statement 21,250: the remaining -58,452 is exactly the printed Adjustments column elimination (gross per fund vs netted Total), which is the expected transfers basis difference, not an error.

gaps.explanation: The only business-type revenue detail line is the budget schedule's mixed 'Local Receipts: Other' 1,327,744 (p20, cash basis, unaudited), which includes the 141,113 governmental receipts listed under the governmental revenue gap; its business part is 1,186,631. The proprietary statement p16 (accrual) prints operating revenues 985,674 + interest 2,891 + sale of assets 76,292 + insurance 4,697 + miscellaneous 5,421 = 1,074,975. The cash-basis figure includes Trash Fund loan proceeds 116,007 and cash receipts from customers 979,218 (cash flow statement p18; cash-flow total receipts 979,218 + 10,118 + 76,292 + 116,007 + 3,318 = 1,184,953, within 1,678 of the budget figure). 1,327,744 - 1,074,975 = 252,769 = gap: governmental receipts 141,113 + cash vs accrual basis (mainly loan proceeds) 111,656. No breakdown printed; no fix.

Business-type spending detail is the budget schedule p21 (cash basis, 'Disbursements and Transfers'): Electric 797,927 + Trash 247,180 + Sewer 142,497 + Water 128,819 = 1,316,423. The statement total 1,003,344 (Statement of Activities p3 = proprietary operating expenses 981,428 + interest 21,916, p16) is accrual: it includes depreciation 114,246 and excludes capital purchases 331,589 and debt principal 80,000 (cash flow p18), which the cash budget includes, along with transfers. Cash-flow outflows 645,262 + 209,422 + 331,589 + 80,000 + 18,672 = 1,284,945, plus Electric transfers out 24,700 = 1,309,645 (within 6,778 of the unaudited budget figure). Gap -313,079 is this basis difference; no lines missing or duplicated.
